claim: A meta-analysis of 11 comparative studies in nontumoral epilepsy (389 LITT vs 557 open surgery) found complete seizure freedom 53.7% after LITT vs 68.1% after open surgery (RR 0.81, p=0.07, not significant), with significantly fewer complications after LITT (18.3% vs 30.0%).

bibliographic_record.authors: Maroufi SF, Fallahi MS, Amirkhani N, Dehghani Arani P, Theodore JN, Cohen-Gadol AA, Sheehan JP, Van Gompel JJ
bibliographic_record.title: Laser interstitial thermal therapy versus open resective surgery for nontumoral epilepsy: systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies

supporting_passage: Open surgery demonstrated higher rates of complete seizure freedom, although not reaching significance (68.1% vs 53.7%, RR 0.81, p = 0.07).
passage_location: Abstract, Results section. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 41576371; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/41576371; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of comparative (non-randomised) studies
population_and_design.population: nontumoral epilepsy (TLE, focal cortical dysplasia, tuberous sclerosis), mixed ages

endpoint.reported_endpoint: complete seizure freedom; 'adequate seizure freedom' secondary

reported_observation: Non-significant trend favouring open surgery for complete seizure freedom; significant in EZ-directed resection subgroup; fewer complications and shorter stay with LITT.
author_inference: Open surgery remains slightly superior for long-term seizure freedom; LITT less invasive with lower morbidity.
contradictions: Ekman 2024 reports significant superiority of resection in MTLE; here overall difference is not significant (p=0.07) and sensitive to influential-study analysis.
overlap_note: Comparative studies likely overlap with Pichardo-Rojas 2026; not independent evidence.
